title: Collagen structure and stability
funder: Collagen research in the authors' laboratory is supported by NIH grant AR044276; M.D.S. was supported by graduate fellowships from the Department of Homeland Security and the Division of Medicinal Chemistry, American Chemical Society.
authorConflicts: The authors are not aware of any affiliations, memberships, funding or financial holdings that might be perceived as affecting the objectivity of the review.
result: Review. Prolyl 4-hydroxylase, a non-haem iron enzyme, hydroxylates proline residues in the Yaa position of collagen Xaa-Yaa-Gly triplets to (2S,4R)-4-hydroxyproline. Hydroxylation of Yaa-position proline increases dramatically the thermal stability of collagen triple helices, and prolyl 4-hydroxylase activity is required for the viability of Caenorhabditis elegans and the mouse.
